title: Learning Chicago stepping dance moves class part 3!

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructor guides couples through Chicago stepping patterns by calling out counts and footwork instructions while dancing with a partner. He emphasizes proper form such as maintaining an L-shape and turning at the correct counts.

lesson_structure.note: Teacher explains and demonstrates footwork and L-shape positioning with partner.
Teacher counts aloud while leading the class through basic cross steps and turns.
Teacher breaks down the boomerang turn step by step.

common_mistakes: Not turning at the right count

steps_taught.name: Cross step
steps_taught.description: Basic stepping pattern crossing feet on the count

steps_taught.name: Boomerang
steps_taught.description: Turning partner movement ending in closed position

what_works: Repetitive counting and clear verbal prompts help learners follow along.
what_hinders: The camera angle from behind foreground students partially obstructs the teacher's footwork.

quotes.text: You should always have an L-shape going on.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher in black shirt explaining foot positioning to students in a studio.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact weight transfer details of background students

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher continuously dances alongside partner while calling out counts and anatomical/geometric shapes like the L-shape.
